target: Determine whether the published P7-free List-3 restriction machinery itself supplies enough information to compile each polynomial restriction into bounded-seed CSZ normal subcases with arbitrary-size X0', while removing all targeted competing vertices from SOURCE Y under axiom (v).
admissible_compilation: Seed size bounded by a function of the original seed size, independent of n.
Arbitrarily large X0' allowed as by the CSZ normal-subcase definition.
Exact preservation of extension existence plus polynomial reconstruction.
Every claimed external list-size reduction used to move a vertex from Y to X must be certified by source L_{P'} or the vertex itself must be legitimately moved to S' or X0'.
pass_terminal: PASS_LIST3_SOURCE_IMPORT: the existing List-3 restriction machinery, without an additional unproved structural theorem, yields source-valid normal subcases in which the targeted competing source-Y vertices disappear while seed remains bounded.
fail_terminal: FAIL_DIRECT_LIST3_SOURCE_IMPORT: there is a semantic step used by the external palette machinery that cannot be represented by source L_P / bounded seed / X0 normal-subcase semantics; importing it would require an additional source-specific theorem or potentially super-polynomial branching.
audit_tests: Compare singleton bulk assignments with CSZ X0' semantics.
Compare palette propagation from X0' with the exact definition of L_{P'}.
Apply axiom (v) and Lemma 10 normalization after the attempted import.
Check whether non-singleton external <=2 palettes can be represented without committing a color.
Do not treat a schematic counterexample as proof that every possible enhanced source-specific bridge is impossible.
